decisions.reason: As a flanged dismantling joint closely related to the firm’s core pipeline and fittings business, it fits existing knowledge and production capabilities, so management would expect it can be improved and sold through established channels despite limited visible R&D signals.

A powder-coated public waste bin is commercially and technologically more distant from the firm’s water-infrastructure offer, and without clear evidence of strong in-house R&D or research cooperation management would see limited absorptive capacity to learn and build an advantage in it.

Although the firm can manufacture and coat metal products, the waste-bin-with-ashtray line sits outside its established customer problem-solving domain, so management would likely reallocate resources to nearer products where its prior knowledge is more useful.

Outdoor public ashtrays are also distant from the firm’s established pipeline-related business, and under an absorptive-capacity view the firm is less likely to keep developing a peripheral line it cannot easily interpret, market, and refine from existing experience.
